extracted.intended_audience: community organizers, advocates, impacted individuals, and counsel preparing public comments on agency rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting public comments on proposed agency rules that both persuade decisionmakers and create a precise factual record for judicial review; includes tactics for mobilizing lived-experience testimony and building collective expertise. Emphasizes strategic purposes beyond immediate persuasion, including standing and evidentiary value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of audience / strategic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should be crafted with awareness of audience. While administrators may dismiss them, courts reviewing agency decisions examine comment records carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor comments with both immediate decisionmakers and potential judicial reviewers in mind. Recognize that material appearing weak or uninformed to one decisionmaker might register as informed evidence to another; therefore balance persuasive rhetoric with record-building detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground comments in real-world expertise and lived experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments should be grounded in real-world expertise and lived experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center submissions on domain knowledge from people who know how a rule will operate on the ground — e.g., counselors, home health aides, advocates. Provide concrete descriptions of day-to-day effects rather than abstract assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilize grassroots expertise / collective commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize community members who possess practical knowledge of policy areas; collective commenting 'claims and affirms this expertise' among populations often excluded from formal political processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage coordinated submissions from affected communities to demonstrate breadth and legitimacy of lived expertise. Use mobilization to surface diverse, consistent accounts that rebut claims of anecdotalism or irrelevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an evidentiary record with precise factual detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments serve as historical documentation of policy impacts; personal testimonies about concrete hardships — 'unpredictable earnings, inaccessible public transportation, unaffordable child care' — create a public archive demonstrating real consequences of agency choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific, concrete facts (examples, timelines, quantifiable harms, local conditions) and firsthand accounts that can be cited in later review or litigation. Avoid vague or generalized claims; document measurable impacts where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve a judicial record / long-term litigation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The immediate goal isn't always persuading current decision-makers; it can be building a judicial record and historical witness to support legal challenge later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize elements that an appellate court would find difficult for an agency to explain away: clear factual assertions, consistent testimony, and documented procedural objections. Understand that a comment that fails politically can still succeed legally if it preserves a precise factual record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use commenting to establish standing and assert authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of commenting itself is constitutive of standing as a knowledgeable participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage participation by affected individuals and groups as a way to assert institutionalized expertise and political presence. Collective comments can help demonstrate that commenters are stakeholders with relevant knowledge and standing to challenge agency action.
